name: Reina Gallagher
life: “I still remember collecting cash in the year nobody had change.” Friday often includes a stop at the public end of the South Shore boardwalk, where Reina checks the shade on the benches before deciding how long to stay.
voice: I collected rent in the rain and swapped the tins. I traced every tenant before closing my books.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a brown corduroy jacket and a knotted piece of sail thread on a key ring. Reina has a broad nose and a deep dimple on one cheek, with short copper curls. Reina listens with the head tilted a little to the left during a conversation.
personality: Reina loves a well-told anecdote and distrusts the neat ending. The parts Reina remembers are the interruptions, unfinished jobs and people who had to go back to work halfway through.
agenda: To match every envelope before month-end.
family: Clement Mitchell is Reina’s cousin. Reina leaves the first voice message. Clement calls back when there is finally a little privacy. In their family a missed ring can mean a bus, a customer, a sleeping child or a bad hour. Neither treats it as an answer in itself. Asked about *Laundry for a stranger*, Clement says, “I can't stand a starched collar since catering school.”
connections: Grey Ibrahim. They get the former dealer a reliable record of which rent was actually collected. Also in the story is Gareth Yeo (budget tutor).

reactions.situation: A family asks to come back later without explanation
reactions.response: Reina arranges a second visit without repeating the family's explanation.
